content.title: Houston airports see highest TSA callout rates in the nation, straining security lines | What travelers need to know
content.text: Travelers in Houston face long security lines at airports due to a staffing shortage among TSA officers amid the DHS shutdown, federal officials report. HOUSTON — Travelers at Bush Intercontinental Airport are facing some of the longest security delays seen during the ongoing federal shutdown — with wait times now reaching up to four hours and conditions changing by the hour. Officials warn the situation could continue to shift throughout the day as TSA staffing shortages persist, forcing checkpoint closures and limiting screening capacity. TSA staffing shortages driving delays The delays come as Transportation Security Administration staffing levels continue to drop during the Department of Homeland Security shutdown. Federal officials say TSA officers have been working without pay since the shutdown began Feb. 14, contributing to a surge in callouts nationwide. New data shows absenteeism rates reached 11.5% on March 21 — the highest recorded during the shutdown. In Houston, the impact has been even more severe. At Bush Intercontinental Airport (IAH), 42.4% of TSA officers reportedly called out, while Hobby Airport saw a 47.4% callout rate. Officials say the shortages are leading to long lines, fewer open screening lanes and rapidly changing conditions at airports across the country. What it looks like on the ground Conditions at Bush Airport appear worse than posted estimates in some areas. At Terminal C earlier in the morning, wait times were listed at 30 minutes, but lines stretched outside the terminal. Similar scenes were reported at Hobby Airport. At Terminal A, lines extended into the lower level near the airport train, with staff controlling how many passengers could move up escalators at a time. That same system was also in place at Terminal E. One traveler with a 1 p.m. flight said they arrived early to avoid delays as lines continued “growing by the minute.” What it looks like inside Bush Airport right now Conditions inside the airport have continued to deteriorate as the morning rush builds. At Terminal E, signage shows wait times of up to 240 minutes — or four hours — to get through security. While traffic outside the airport may not appear severe, travelers say the situation inside is far more chaotic, with lines stretching throughout terminals, into baggage claim areas and even outside the building. By mid-morning, only two TSA checkpoints remained open — one in Terminal A and one in Terminal E — after the Terminal C checkpoint shut down around 9:15 a.m. Video from KHOU 11 crews shows ICE agents positioned near security checkpoints in Terminal E, assisting as crowds continue to grow. Some travelers say confusion is making the situation worse, pointing to unclear communication and outdated signage. One passenger who arrived from an international flight said he went searching for a TSA PreCheck line, only to find it had already closed — leaving him stuck in a much longer standard line. “Sometimes you make mistakes and you don’t know if you can fix or not… how was I supposed to know I was going into the worst line in airport history in my 30 whatever years of life,” the traveler said. What’s changed this morning at Bush Airport Houston Airports says conditions may continue to shift throughout the day depending on staffing. Travelers flying United are being told to check bags at Terminal C, then proceed to Terminal E for security screening. Officials say screening lanes may open or close throughout the day based on staffing levels, which can cause sudden spikes in wait times. Passengers are encouraged to stay in contact with their airlines for possible rebooking options if delays impact travel plans. What travelers should know before heading to the airport Operational changes remain in place that could impact wait times: At Bush Airport: TSA PreCheck is limited and will close at all terminals at 10:30 a.m.Standard screening is available in Terminals A, C and E, though availability may changeCLEAR is not operating Monday At Hobby Airport: Fewer screening lanes are open, which may increase wait times Officials warn wait times at Bush Airport could exceed four hours at times. Federal response and ICE presence Federal officials say the Trump administration is deploying additional resources to airports experiencing the most disruption. That includes ICE agents, who have been spotted at Bush Airport and are assisting with crowd management near security checkpoints. Officials say decisions about ICE personnel and their roles are made at the federal level. ‘We’re suffering’: Travelers react to long waits Passengers say the delays are taking a toll. “Everybody’s pissed off, but I mean, what are you going to do about it, really? Just got to kind of go with the flow and see what happens,” said one traveler waiting in a security line expected to take hours. Others say the shutdown is impacting both travelers and workers. “The people that are receiving these services… we’re suffering as well, and you can already see the long lines, the long waits and the inefficiency that has come about,” another traveler said. What happens next Officials say travelers should plan ahead, arrive early and be prepared for delays as the situation continues to evolve. With staffing shortages ongoing, conditions at Bush Airport — and airports across the country — could remain unpredictable. Got a news tip or story idea?
